title: Fallback orchestra and autoresolve sketch
content:
Purpose and scope:
This scratchpad defines a cross-functional pattern for coordinating multiple fallback mechanisms when an LLM rollout encounters degradation. The goal is to provide a low-friction orchestration layer (the 'fallback orchestra') that composes automated fallbacks, human handoffs, and graceful autoresolve behavior so experiments can fail fast but recover without manual toil.

Principles (high level):
- Least surprise: end-users should see minimal disruption; fallback should prefer conservative behaviors (delay, degrade, rerank) before full rollback.
- Observable and reversible: every automated fallback action must emit a discrete telemetry event and be reversible via the console or API.
- Team-aware: fallbacks carry metadata (owner, experiment id, slice) so the steward can be paged with context.
- Cheap first: prefer cheaper mitigations (reduce generation length, quantize variant, fall back to cached replies) before capacity-heavy options.

Fallback bands (rough taxonomy):
1) Local mitigation (no traffic routing changes): token limit reduction, safety-filter bypass gating, local cache hit, smaller-model proxy.
2) Routing fallback: shift percentage to a stable variant (v-small or cached), route by region/tier.
3) Degrade features: turn off nonessential post-processing (reranking, tool-calling) to reclaim headroom.
4) Full rollback: revert rollout config and restore previous release.

Trigger signals (examples):
- User-perceived latency P90 > SLO by 20% sustained for 5m
- Error-rate spike (5xx or model-level hallucination metric) exceeding threshold for 3m
- Safety classifier breach counts across top slices
- Cost per request > budgeted unit cost by 40% for a sustained window

Orchestration flow (sketch):
1) Detection: signal fires -> create incident run with experiment metadata.
2) Local mitigation: apply 'band-1' mitigations automatically (token cap, query-sampling), emit events.
3) Evaluate: 3-minute rolling window; if metrics improve -> schedule autoresolve (grace period 30m).
4) Escalate: if no improvement -> shift 10% traffic to stable variant (routing band), page steward with snapshot + recovery actions.
5) Human decision point: on-call can approve full rollback or continue staged exposure.

Autoresolve semantics:
- Conditions to autoresolve: metrics return within safe band for two consecutive evaluation windows and no safety violations for the grace period.
- Autoresolve actions must document: what changed, who was paged, why it resolved, and include a link to the playbook.
- If autoresolve triggers and then re-fires within 2 hours, mark experiment as unstable and require manual review.

Telemetry and observability checklist (must emit):
- fallback.event {type, experiment_id, slice, action, reason, before_metrics, after_metrics}
- traffic.partition.snapshot {percentages, routing_version}
- autoresolve.event {experiment_id, condition_met, window_summary}
- ticket.link if human intervention created a tracked issue

Oncall and comms:
- Page payload must include top-3 diagnostic signals, minimal reproduction steps, relevant logs link, and steering actions available from console.
- If routed to SRE/product steward, include recommended next steps: increase shard capacity, disable reranker, rollback.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Where do fallback policies live in git vs console? recommend: policy JSON in repo + editable override in console.
- Need simulation harness to run synthetic traffic that exercises cascade scenarios (latency + hallucination combined).
- Define authority matrix for who can autoresolve automatically (default: experiment owner + release engineer).
- UX for visible fallback state in console (banner vs full incident card).

Immediate next actions (owners):
- (Aisha) prototype telemetry schema + minimal event producer hooks (due 2025-02-01).
- (Daniel) spike for a small routing shim that can shift 10% in <30s and emit snapshots (due 2025-02-08).
- (Marta) mockup console banner and autoresolve flow for review (due 2025-02-05).

Notes to self: keep this intentionally experimental — prefer iterate-and-learn. Link this sketch into the broader rollouts playbook once validated in canary lab.

Appendix: quick scenario (example):
- A/B test of reranker enabled on 20% traffic. Latency P95 for reranker slice increases 80ms -> trigger local mitigation: token cap + disable heavy rerank scoring (band-1). Metrics improve marginally -> after 6m still above threshold -> routing fallback applied (shift 15% back to non-reranked). Pager fires with snapshot. Oncall approves autoresolve after 40m when metrics stabilize; autoresolve rolls back routing shift over 10 minutes and annotates runbook. If instability repeats, block further auto-exposure for 24h.
